visual.general_description: Twelve-lead ECG printed on pink grid paper with lead labels and a bottom rhythm strip.
visual.detailed_description: Color scan of an ECG printout on pink millimetre-style grid paper. The tracing area holds three rows of four lead columns plus a fourth long strip along the bottom. Printed labels read I, II and III at the left of the three rows, aVR, aVL and aVF in the second column, V1, V2 and V3 in the third column, and V4, V5 and V6 in the fourth column; the long bottom strip carries a label at its left end that reads II. Small rectangular calibration pulses sit at the left end of each row. Every row shows small, regularly repeating complexes along a near-flat baseline, with larger downward complexes in the V1 to V3 columns. A thin vertical dark line crosses the tracing area between the third and fourth lead columns. No patient name, identifier, date, time, device text, speed, gain or rate readout is printed.

caption_claims.value: Caption states the image is the ECG upon admission.

limitations: Rhythm, rate and intervals were not read from the pixels; sinus tachycardia is the authors statement.
Resolution is about 767 by 432 pixels, too low to read small deflections reliably.
